supportingEvidence.title: Reuters: Iran-Oman corridor talks resume while a tanker is struck near the Strait entrance
supportingEvidence.note: Reports a proposed joint temporary navigational corridor and mine clearing, while also reporting a tanker disabled by an unidentified projectile near Oman the same day.

supportingEvidence.title: Reuters: Brent extends losses on hopes of Hormuz reopening
supportingEvidence.note: Brent fell to about $86.80 and WTI to about $80.87 as markets priced de-escalation/reopening optimism.

supportingEvidence.title: Oman Foreign Ministry: temporary maritime-corridor mechanism for Hormuz
supportingEvidence.note: Primary Omani background confirms an established policy and coordination mechanism for temporary corridor access and freedom of navigation.

contradictingEvidence.title: Reuters: diplomatic progress remains incomplete and passage remains perilous
contradictingEvidence.note: The talks themselves could still produce an operational corridor quickly; one attack may be an isolated event rather than evidence that the broader reopening path is failing.

falsifier: A sustained multi-day rise in independent vessel throughput, declining war-risk/freight premiums, no further maritime attacks, and restored refined-product deliveries make incident-level security data add no predictive value over the public corridor-talk and oil-price baseline.

evidence.title: Reuters reporting on tanker strike near Oman and Hormuz corridor talks

title: Hormuz reopening optimism diverges from physical security after fresh tanker strike
summary: Markets and diplomacy are shifting toward reopening optimism, but a fresh tanker strike near the Strait entrance shows the physical-security state has not normalized. Narrative, price, and incident-level evidence are diverging.
delta: Refine CONTESTED_REOPENING into a two-layer state: diplomatic/market de-escalation is improving, while physical maritime-security confirmation remains incomplete. Do not advance to NORMALIZING until throughput, attack frequency, freight, insurance, and product-delivery data confirm the move.
firstOrderImpacts: continued downside pressure on oil risk premium if talks progress
persistent war-risk and freight uncertainty despite lower crude prices
greater value of incident-level maritime monitoring for validating reopening
secondOrderImpacts: possible divergence between crude-price optimism and shipping/insurance economics
lower energy-inflation expectations could reverse quickly if attacks continue
alternative-data value shifts toward measuring realized physical security rather than summarizing diplomatic statements

alphaHunter.hypothesis: Incident-level maritime security plus independent vessel/freight data will identify failed or fragile reopening states earlier than diplomatic statements and Brent price action alone.
alphaHunter.baseline: Iran-Oman corridor statements plus Brent/WTI reaction
alphaHunter.alternativeData: UKMTO/JMIC incident events, independent vessel throughput, war-risk insurance, tanker freight, and refined-product delivery data
alphaHunter.incrementalValueMetric: 3-7 day forecast error for confirmed throughput/security normalization versus the public diplomatic/price baseline
alphaHunter.killCondition: Kill the extra data layer if it fails to improve held-out reopening-state forecasts or arrives too late to change a research decision.
